findings.text:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hash overridden style bodies in the sizer cache key**

When a `[[leaves.sizer_escalation]]` overrides `style_file`, the escalation tuple hashes only the configured path while this block reads bytes only from `cfg.sizer.style_file`. After a verdict has been cached, editing the escalation-specific style therefore leaves `_sizer_key` unchanged, so `run_sizer` returns the old verdict without rerunning either pass and the updated style never takes effect. Include the resolved body of every escalation-specific style in the cache key as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.text:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep style text out of flag-deduplication scans**

When a Claude style body contains text such as `--effort` (for example in documentation or a code snippet), adding the arbitrary body to `argv` before `_mapped_argv` makes its substring-based probe mistake that prompt text for an explicit CLI flag. The configured effort is then silently omitted, so a styled planner/signoff/act leaf can run at the vendor default instead of its pinned tier. Compute mapped flags against the real configured option arguments before appending the style payload, or otherwise exclude option values from the deduplication scan.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.text:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound the Claude style argument before spawning**

When an instance points `style_file` at a sufficiently large Markdown file, the entire body becomes one command-line argument with no size check. This exceeds Windows' whole-command-line limit at roughly 32 KiB and Linux's per-argument limit around 128 KiB, causing the subprocess spawn itself to fail before the leaf runs; the nearby interactive seed path already guards against these limits, but it does not cover this separate argument. Use a bounded/file-backed transport or fail open for oversized style bodies.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.text:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle symlink-loop errors while resolving styles**

On the supported Python 3.11 and 3.12 runtimes, `Path.resolve()` raises `RuntimeError` for a symlink loop rather than either exception caught here. If a configured style path is or traverses a circular symlink, `_resolve_style` therefore crashes planner/signoff/act invocation—and can also escape the advisory sizer's normal failure containment—instead of following the documented fail-open behavior for unreadable style files. Catch `RuntimeError` as well so this configuration degrades to no styling.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

findings.author: eduralph
findings.text: Fixed in da47bd6 — the style body now joins argv only AFTER `_mapped_argv`'s scan, so prompt payload never takes part in option-dedup decisions. Pinned by a composition trace through the real `_invoke` with the spawn stubbed (`test_mapped_flags_survive_a_style_body_that_mentions_them`).

findings.author: eduralph
findings.text: Fixed in a2baa3c (bounded, fail-open with a stderr note) and tightened in da47bd6: the bound now reuses the seed's per-platform budget from #313 (`_SEED_ARG_BUDGET`, ~96 KiB Linux / ~24 KiB Windows), which covers the Windows whole-command-line case as well. The inline (codex-reviewer) branch keeps big bodies — a prompt has no per-argument limit.

findings.author: eduralph
findings.text: Fixed in da47bd6 — `_resolve_style` catches RuntimeError alongside OSError/ValueError, with a real two-link-loop regression test (it exercises the OSError arm on 3.13+ and the RuntimeError arm on 3.11/3.12). Note the same latent shape exists upstream in `rubric._resolve`; left to the template side, since that file is not part of this delta's surface.
